issues.display_title: Issue #416: Loading spinner never clears when a texture URL returns 404
issues.main_description_html:
Symptom

When a texture URL returns HTTP 404, the gallery's loading spinner never disappears. The viewer is stuck on the loading state permanently — no error, no timeout, no console rejection. Text walls are also affected: their textures can fail to appear with no diagnostic.

Root cause

Three separate promises in the texture-loading path can never settle. Any one of them is enough to hang the whole load. All three are on the same failure mode: an unhappy path that simply has no code attached to it.

A. fetchTextureFile rejection is dropped — this is the 404 path

main.service.ts:938

loadTexture(textureSource: any, forSceneEnv = false, scene: any = null) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const texureHasLoaded = () => resolve(texture);
    const failedToLoadTexture = (err: any) => reject(err);

    let texture: any = null;

    this.fetchTextureFile(textureSource).then((fileSource: any) => {
      // ... new BABYLON.Texture(fileSource, scene, ..., texureHasLoaded, failedToLoadTexture)
    });
  });
}

fetchTextureFile does reject correctly on an HTTP error — main.service.ts:1023, error: (err: any) => reject(err).

But loadTexture attaches only .then() to it. No .catch, no second argument, no reject forwarding. So when the HTTP request 404s:

  1. fetchTextureFile rejects.
  2. The .then callback never runs, so new BABYLON.Texture(...) is never constructed.
  3. failedToLoadTexture is therefore never wired to anything — it is defined, but only ever passed to a BABYLON.Texture that does not exist yet.
  4. The outer new Promise is never resolved or rejected. It stays pending forever.

The reject handler exists and looks like error handling, which is why this reads as safe. It only covers a decode failure after the bytes arrived. It does not cover the bytes never arriving.

B. utils.service.loadTexture has no error path at all

utils.service.ts:433

public loadTexture(url: string, scene: any): Promise<any> {
  return new Promise((resolve, _) => {
    const texture = new BABYLON.Texture(url, scene);
    texture.onLoadObservable.add(() => {
      resolve(texture);
    });
  });
}

The reject parameter is discarded (_). Only onLoadObservable is subscribed, and Babylon never fires that observable for a texture that failed to load. On 404 this promise is pending forever.

This is the one on the text wall path, and it is reached twice:

  • text-loader.service.ts:91 — _createTextMaterial, the initial text wall texture
  • text-loader.service.ts:53 — changeQuality, the quality upgrade

Note that the sibling implementation in main.service.ts (A above) does pass onError to the BABYLON.Texture constructor. Two implementations of the same job, one wires the error callback and one does not.

C. fetchTextureFile also hangs on an empty body

main.service.ts:1015

} else if (event instanceof HttpResponse) {
  const arrayBuffer: ArrayBuffer | null = event.body;
  if (arrayBuffer) {
    // ... resolve(blobUrl);
  }
}

If the response body is null or empty, the if is skipped, the observable completes, and nothing resolves or rejects. Pending forever. A 200 with an empty body hangs exactly like a 404 does.

Why the spinner never clears

villume-gallery.component.ts:846-894

this.mainService.scene.onReadyObservable.add(() => {
  this.mainService.loadExhibtion().then(async () => {
    // ...
    await this.loadAllArtwork();
    await this.loadAllText();

    if (this.mainService.ordinaryObjects.length != 0) {
      this.loadAllOrdinaryObject();
    } else {
      this.mainService.allAssetsHasLoaded = true;
    }
    // ...
  });
});

loadExhibtion awaits loadTexture for the lightmap at main.service.ts:5242 and for the scene environment at main.service.ts:5513. With defect A, that await never returns, so loadExhibtion() never settles and the entire .then block never runs.

allAssetsHasLoaded stays false, and the spinner is bound directly to it — villume-gallery.component.html:325:

@if (!mainService.allAssetsHasLoaded) {
  <div class="place-spinner">

There is also no .catch on this chain. So even after A, B and C are fixed so the promises reject properly, the spinner would still stay up forever — the rejection would just become an unhandled promise rejection. A rejecting promise and a pending promise look identical to the user here. Both need addressing.

The lightmap call at 5242 sits inside a try { } block, which is worth calling out: the try cannot help, because a promise that never settles never throws. The error handling that is present is unreachable, not wrong.

Reproduction

Not yet reproduced in a browser — this is a code trace, and should be confirmed against a live gallery before the fix is signed off.

Expected repro: point light_map (or any text wall picture_* field) at a URL that 404s, load the gallery, observe the spinner never clears and no error surfaces in the console.

Suggested direction

Not implemented — filing for triage first.

  1. Forward the rejection in main.service.loadTexture: give the fetchTextureFile(...) chain a .catch(failedToLoadTexture), or use .then(onOk, failedToLoadTexture).
  2. Give utils.service.loadTexture an error path — pass onError to the BABYLON.Texture constructor and call reject, matching what main.service.loadTexture already does. Consider deleting the duplicate entirely and routing text walls through the single implementation.
  3. Reject in fetchTextureFile when HttpResponse arrives with no body, instead of falling through.
  4. Add a .catch to the loadExhibtion().then(...) chain that clears the loading state and surfaces the failure, so a texture that genuinely cannot load degrades to a visible error rather than an infinite spinner.

Worth deciding as part of triage: should one missing texture be fatal to the whole gallery load, or should it be logged and skipped so the rest of the exhibition still renders? That choice determines whether the fix belongs at the loadTexture call sites or at the top-level catch.

Why the lint gate did not catch this

It cannot. ng lint and tsc --noEmit both pass on all of this — every promise is well typed and every branch is syntactically fine. The bug is entirely in the paths that have no code, which no static check can see.

Related: @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises would not have caught it either, since the promises here are awaited, not dropped.

Note — text walls are missing because of the backend data, not this bug

Verified against a live gallery (Y7S3x1ee) on 2026-07-31.

The API returns six text walls and none of them carry a picture field. The string "picture" does not appear anywhere in the viewer payload:

text_walls count: 6
[0] id=3ce3b0c4-c0f2-4eb5-b106-0822ce5c9d63 picture=undefined
    keys: color, content, deleted, font_family, font_size, font_style, id,
          line_height, name, position, rotation, scaling,
          text_horizontal_alignment, text_vertical_alignment

text.picture is therefore undefined, and _getTextsDataFromExhibitionData builds the URL from it anyway:

path passed to convertPathImage = "undefined?resize=50x50"
base64('local:///undefined')    = bG9jYWw6Ly8vdW5kZWZpbmVk
URL   = https://img2.villume.com/v/rs:fit:50:50:no:0/cb:.../bG9jYWw6Ly8vdW5kZWZpbmVk
curl  = 404

Confirmed by request, six times, one per wall. Artworks are unaffected because their image field is populated (.../446e84c50206b689.png?resize=1024x585), which is why paintings render and text walls do not.

A text wall is rendered purely from its pre-rendered picture — _createTextMaterial loads the texture and _createTextContentWrapper only builds an empty plane. There is no native text-rendering path, even though the payload carries every ingredient (content, font_family, font_size, color, line_height, alignment). The TextWall interface declares picture: string as non-optional, so TypeScript trusts a contract the API does not honour.

The frontend cannot fix this. The error handling described above only changes how it fails — from an infinite spinner into a clean skip. The text will stay invisible until either:

  1. the backend generates and returns picture for text walls, or
  2. the frontend renders text natively from content via BABYLON.DynamicTexture — a new feature, not a bug fix.

Worth splitting into a separate backend issue.

issues.display_title: Issue #417: fix: splash screen button position and header text width
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Splash screen preview did not render correctly: the CTA button sat slightly too low when using the centered position variant, and long header text wrapped/clipped inconsistently because the heading had no explicit width.

Fixed in commit fc25782.

Changes

splash-screen-preview.component.scss

  • .position-3: bottom: 50% → bottom: 53% so the button lines up with the centered layout.
  • .header: added width: 100% so header text takes the full container width instead of shrinking to the inline-block content box.

splash-screen-preview.component.html

  • Reformatted the template (mobile + desktop blocks) — the previous indentation of @if / @else blocks was broken and hard to read.
  • Note: the mobile CTA still has a duplicated class="btn" attribute (see below).

Follow-up

The mobile button keeps a duplicate attribute that should be cleaned up:

<button class="btn" class="btn" [ngStyle]="{visibility:'visible'}" ...>

Files

  • src/app/components/splash-screen-preview/splash-screen-preview.component.scss
  • src/app/components/splash-screen-preview/splash-screen-preview.component.html
